questions.question: According to the chapter, what is the primary purpose of the research literature in psychology?

answers.text: To provide self-help advice for the general public
To serve as a source of new research questions and a repository of published findings
To replace the need for new empirical studies
To offer encyclopedia entries on psychological topics

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT identified in the chapter as a common source of research ideas?

answers.text: Informal observations
Practical problems
Previous research
Personal horoscopes

questions.question: What does the chapter say about Wikipedia as a source for scientific research?

answers.text: It is a highly reliable peer-reviewed source
It is unsuitable because authors are anonymous and content changes
It should be the primary source for literature reviews
It is acceptable if used alongside professional journals

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is double-blind peer review?

answers.text: A process where reviewers and authors do not know each other's identities
A review conducted by two editors simultaneously
A method where only the editor knows the author's identity
A review process conducted without reading the manuscript

questions.question: Which database does the chapter identify as the most important for searching psychology research literature?

answers.text: ERIC
PubMed
PsycINFO
JSTOR

questions.question: What does the chapter recommend regarding how recent sources should be for a literature review?

answers.text: Always use sources from the past 50 years
Focus on sources from the past five years, with exceptions for classic articles
Only use sources published in the current year
Age of sources does not matter in psychology

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is a theory in scientific research?

answers.text: An untested wild guess about a phenomenon
A coherent explanation of phenomena that goes beyond direct observation
A specific prediction about what will happen in a study
A collection of unrelated facts

questions.question: What is a hypothesis as defined in the chapter?

answers.text: A broad explanation of multiple phenomena
A specific prediction about a new phenomenon that should be observed if a theory is accurate
A general research idea before any testing
An alternative term for a research question

questions.question: What does the hypothetico-deductive method involve?

answers.text: Constructing a theory, deriving a hypothesis, testing it, and reevaluating the theory
Testing multiple theories without deriving hypotheses
Collecting data before formulating any theory
Proving theories through single experiments

questions.question: According to the chapter, which characteristic is NOT required for a good hypothesis?

answers.text: It must be testable and falsifiable
It must be logical and informed by previous research
It must predict that a relationship does not exist
It must make a positive statement about the existence of a relationship

questions.question: What is the difference between quantitative and categorical variables?

answers.text: Quantitative variables are qualities, while categorical variables are quantities
Quantitative variables are measured with numbers, while categorical variables are qualities assigned category labels
There is no difference between them
Quantitative variables cannot be measured

questions.question: What is an operational definition?

answers.text: A definition that describes how a variable will be precisely measured
A theoretical explanation of a construct
A general description of a research topic
A synonym for hypothesis

questions.question: According to the chapter, what is the primary advantage of experimental research over non-experimental research?

answers.text: It is easier to conduct
It allows researchers to determine causal relationships
It requires fewer participants
It is always conducted in natural settings

questions.question: What is a confound in experimental research?

answers.text: Any variable other than the dependent variable
An extraneous variable that varies systematically with the independent variable
The variable that the experimenter measures
A variable that is intentionally manipulated

questions.question: What does the chapter say about the relationship between internal and external validity?

answers.text: They are always positively correlated
There is typically a trade-off; high internal validity often means low external validity
They are unrelated concepts
External validity is always more important than internal validity

questions.question: Which of the following is a measure of central tendency?

answers.text: Standard deviation
Range
Mean
Variance

questions.question: What is the purpose of inferential statistics?

answers.text: To summarize data from a sample
To determine whether findings are statistically significant and can be generalized to a population
To calculate the mean of a distribution
To organize data into categories

questions.question: What is a Type I error?

answers.text: Concluding there is no effect when there actually is one in the population
Concluding there is an effect when in reality there is none (false positive)
Using the wrong statistical test
Failing to collect enough data

questions.question: According to the chapter, why do scientists avoid the word 'prove' when discussing theories?

answers.text: Because it sounds too informal
Because results may reflect errors, other theories may explain the same findings, and theories are always subject to revision
Because theories can never be tested
Because the word 'prove' is not in the scientific vocabulary

questions.question: What are the two most prestigious ways to report research findings mentioned in the chapter?

answers.text: Publishing in peer-reviewed journals and presenting at conferences
Writing blog posts and creating podcasts
Publishing in popular magazines and writing self-help books
Posting on social media and creating YouTube videos
